frontier.hypothesis: local-alloc's optimize_reg_copy_1 / optimize_reg_copy_2 are a byte-free reference-TRANSFER dial for any pseudo pair confined to ONE basic block, and can be aimed at a COMPETITOR of out2 (pa4, or the block-2/loop2 allocnos) rather than at out2 itself.
frontier.mechanism: Both routines replace uses of one pseudo with another between a copy insn and the source's death, moving reg_n_refs by loop_depth per replaced use (local-alloc.c:781/783 and 913/914) and adjusting reg_live_length (820 subtracts from the source, 831 adds to the destination) — all AFTER flow has counted and AFTER sched1 has recounted, i.e. exactly at global_alloc's input. No session has ever used this. On the candidate chassis the honest defect is pa4 at 7 refs / live 95 = 1473 outranking a 3-reference out2 (ceiling 731 at live 41), and line 831's d_length addition is the only known way to LENGTHEN pa4 without emitting bytes.
